Python diagnosis and targeted repair

Unit 3 · Week 1 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Use the Unit 3 Week 1 student workbook and separate public teacher key at slides/practice/u3-week1/. Download the companion ZIP; extract before running. Python 3; Lesson 2 additionally uses the existing pygame/pygame-teaching-pack.zip and its pinned requirements. Read the unit3-fluency chapter and foundations workbook. Use fictional values and disposable history files only. No extra assessment or homework. Suggested 55-minute plans are untrialled; select one repair rather than completing every extension.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

Week 1 practical resources

Follow the slide order; preserve each unaided response before opening its feedback.

Student workbook · Separate public teacher key · Download practical files · Four editable decks and resources

1. Python diagnosis and targeted repair

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

2027 teaching edition; retrieval of Year 11 prerequisites, not a new assessment. Keep diagnostic responses separate from later corrections. All resources and keys are public; record prior exposure.

2. An independent starting point

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent diagnostic

Use workbook D1–D4 without running code or opening the key. D1 uses this code; D2 checks a returned result, D3 classifies three faults, D4 selects boundary/empty tests. Record unaided, supported or previously seen. Stop and preserve responses before the next slide. Do not infer a grade from this short sample.

3. Feedback after the diagnostic

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Item-level feedback

Only reveal after original work is preserved. D2 returns 2 while caller count remains 10. D3 missing colon: SyntaxError; int("two"): ValueError at runtime; >5 in an inclusive rule: logic fault. An empty list does not execute the loop. Ask students to explain a mismatch before giving the next step; use teacher key D1–D4.

4. A count changes at the condition

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example with prediction pauses

Trace [4,5,7]: start0; after4=0, after5=1, after7=2. Hide the final row until students predict it. Resetting count inside the loop loses earlier matches. Connect to the allocated exit check. Use a paper trace if Python is unavailable.

5. One repair, with less support

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Faded support and peer explanation

Use workbook R1/R2/R3; choose the weakest diagnostic item, not all three. R1 remove the suggested predicate; R2 repair a missing return; R3 isolate a runtime conversion from a logic comparison. Retain expected/actual and smallest failing example. Secure students may compare local rebinding with list mutation using foundations workbook D; this is optional.

6. A changed unaided check

Suggested time: 8 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent transfer

Fresh values and threshold: expected3 and0. Ask students to write or trace a function without the model; record any help. An immediate retry is formative evidence, not proof of lasting mastery. If boundary fails, compare >= and > using exactly6 before another changed retry.

7. Evidence for the next repair

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Error analysis

Use workbook record: item, expected, actual, explanation, help, next step. Avoid only writing careless mistake. Group students for Lesson2 by observed needs. A student with no previous Pygame experience starts with stage1 and teacher modelling; do not assume prior use.

8. Exit: count and empty input

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Exit ticket

Allocated check u3-l1:2 and0; initialise before iteration; include exact boundary. Collect an unaided explanation. Revisit a changed count during later retrieval within existing lessons; no added homework.
